title.rendered: Peace: The Fruit of the Spirit | Day 3

excerpt.rendered: The Hebrew shalom and the Greek eirēnē do not mean the absence of trouble. They mean the presence of wholeness. A deep structural rightness in the soul the storms cannot touch.

content.rendered:
The English word “peace” is much thinner than what the Bible actually means when it uses the word. The Hebrew shalom and the Greek eirēnē do not mean the absence of trouble. They mean the presence of wholeness. And that is the fruit the Holy Spirit is producing in the believer today.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, September 26, 2026 | The Fruit of the Spirit, Day 3

Today’s Scripture

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.”
Galatians 5:22-23 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

The English word “peace” is much thinner than what the Bible actually means when it uses the word. In modern usage, peace tends to mean the absence of conflict. Quiet. Stillness. A period when nothing is going wrong. That is a real kind of peace, but it is not the peace Jesus offered His disciples in the upper room, and it is not the peace the Holy Spirit produces as the third fruit in Galatians 5:22. The Greek word Paul uses is eirēnē. It is the New Testament equivalent of the Hebrew shalom, one of the richest words in the whole Old Testament vocabulary. Shalom does not mean the absence of trouble. It means the presence of wholeness. Everything in its right place. Everything as it was designed to be. A deep, structural rightness in the soul that does not depend on the surface being smooth.

This is why Paul, writing from a Roman prison awaiting trial for his life, could say to the Philippians, “Be anxious for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God; and the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus” (Philippians 4:6-7 NKJV). The peace Paul is naming is not the absence of the trial. He is still on trial. The peace Paul is naming is a supernatural wholeness in his soul that the trial cannot touch. That peace, he says, surpasses understanding. It cannot be explained by the circumstances. It can only be explained by the Spirit.

The Passion Translation captures the character of this fruit beautifully: “But the fruit produced by the Holy Spirit within you is divine love in all its varied expressions: joy that overflows, peace that subdues, patience that endures, kindness in action” (Galatians 5:22-23 TPT). Peace that subdues. Not peace that hides in a corner. Not peace that waits for the storm to pass. Peace that actively subdues, calms, orders, stabilises the internal chaos of the believer’s world. The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “But the fruit of the (Holy) Spirit [the work which His presence within accomplishes] is love, joy (gladness), peace” (Galatians 5:22 AMPC).

The peace the Spirit produces is not a mood. It is not the mental technique of positive thinking. It is a fruit. A produced thing. A supernatural work of the Holy Spirit in a heart that has been rooted in Christ. That is why the same believer who was anxious yesterday can be at peace today without the circumstances changing. The circumstances are not the source. The Spirit is the source. And He is producing this fruit in every believer who will yield to His work, feed on the Word, and return to the finished work of the cross for the anchor of their soul.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the peace the Spirit is producing in you. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, if you have been anxious this week, do not try to talk yourself out of the anxiety with willpower. Root yourself in Christ. Bring your requests to the Father with thanksgiving. And let the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, guard your heart and mind through Christ Jesus. That is not you working up peace. That is the Spirit growing it in you. Let Him.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that peace is a fruit of Your Spirit in my life. Not the absence of trouble. The presence of wholeness. A deep, structural rightness in my soul that the storms of the surface cannot touch. Today I refuse to try to manufacture peace through willpower. I root myself in Christ. I bring my anxieties to You with thanksgiving. And I trust Your promise. The peace that surpasses understanding guards my heart and mind through Christ Jesus. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Peace is the fruit of the Spirit in my life today. My peace is not the absence of trouble. It is the presence of wholeness. The peace that surpasses understanding guards my heart and mind through Christ Jesus.
